get.description: The grid editor's rows. ``archived=true`` adds the archived ones back.

Find a word by any of the words it is written with.

Searches both printed sides, the spellings it also accepts, its note, its
heading and its lesson's title, and it finds suspended words on purpose —
a word set aside is exactly the one you cannot otherwise get back to.

post.description: Archiving keeps the cards and the log — the note only leaves practice.

get.description:
What is wrong with the collection as practice would meet it (read-only).

The same report ``memo audit`` prints, minus the hints: a screen that
interrupts you should do it for something broken, not for something that
might be. Two notes glossed the same way make an unanswerable prompt, and
the extractor produces them honestly — so this has to be visible from the
app rather than from a command nobody remembers to run.

Other words in the collection with something to do with this one.

Out of what is already written down, so it can offer words that mean the
same or nearly the same thing, and whether the two already accept each
other — not antonyms, which nothing in a note records.

post.description: Write the readable copy of the collection (PLAN 5: manual, never automatic).

patch.description: Change where a staged job will land, before it is committed.

delete.description: Throw a staged job away — the draft and the photos it was read from.

get.description: Uploaded photos, for the review screen. Never serves outside ``var/raw``.

What to practise now, and how long a sitting of it will take.

``drill`` asks for everything in scope, due or not, instead of what the
schedule wanted today — still capped by ``limit``. It is only half of a
drill: how a missed word comes back is the client's own loop.

``direction`` asks a two-sided note only one way round — ``fwd`` for its
front, ``rev`` for its back. A one-way note has no other side, so it is
absent from the direction it does not have rather than asked backwards.

``list_id`` drills one list: every word on it, due or not. Without one,
a list whose focus is still running leads the sitting instead, and the
rest of it is filled exactly as it always was.

``tz_offset`` is the client's minutes ahead of UTC, for the same reason
``/progress`` takes it: the pace counts answers per day, and an evening
sitting that crosses UTC midnight is one sitting, not two.

post.description:
Answers earned with no server to tell — a phone out of reach (PLAN 5).

The same batch may arrive twice, by wire and by file; ``client_id`` is what
keeps that from counting twice.

get.description:
What is known, what keeps going wrong, and what was answered when.

``tz_offset`` is the client's minutes ahead of UTC, so the activity grid
is drawn in the days the person actually practised in.

The whole of one of the lists the Progress page shows a glimpse of.

``bucket`` is a standing — ``new``, ``learning``, ``known``, ``mastered``
— or ``set-aside``, which is not one: a word deliberately left out of
practice, and until this existed the only way back to one was to remember
which lesson it came from. ``file`` keeps one lesson, ``category`` one
category and everything under it.

One lesson in full, for the screen Progress drills down to.

Its counts, the same counts per heading, and every word in it under the
bucket it is in — one read of the log for all of it.
Every list, the focused ones first.

patch.description:
Rename a list, re-date its focus, or end it.

A field left out of the body is left alone; a field sent as null is
cleared, which is how a focus is ended rather than merely forgotten.

delete.description: Forget the set. The words, their marks and their history stay as they are.

post.description: Add words: these ones, or a whole lesson, or one heading of one.

AnswerRowIn.title: AnswerRowIn
AnswerRowIn.description: An answer earned with no server to tell: it brings its own id and its own clock.

AuditFindingOut.title: AuditFindingOut
AuditFindingOut.description: Notes that belong together in a way nobody asked for.

AuditOut.title: AuditOut
AuditOut.description:
What is wrong with the collection as practice would meet it.

``clean`` is defined from the first three only. The last two are hints that
the CLI has always printed and the API used to compute and throw away: a
screen should not *interrupt* for them, but ``near`` is the same signal that
answers "what else do I know that means this", so dropping it was a waste.

CategoryPatch.title: CategoryPatch
CategoryPatch.description: Any subset; ``parent_id`` is set to null to make the category a root.

DuplicateRow.title: DuplicateRow
DuplicateRow.description: Duplicates found for one row of what was sent, by its index.

ExportIn.title: ExportIn
ExportIn.description: Empty exports the whole collection; a category exports that subtree.

FileMasteryOut.title: FileMasteryOut
FileMasteryOut.description: One lesson's four buckets, under the category it belongs to.

FileProgressOut.title: FileProgressOut
FileProgressOut.description: One lesson in full: its counts, each heading's, and its words by bucket.

GroupMasteryOut.title: GroupMasteryOut
GroupMasteryOut.description: One heading of a lesson. ``key`` is null for the notes under no heading.

ImportJobPatch.title: ImportJobPatch
ImportJobPatch.description:
Where a staged job is headed. Unset fields are left alone; an explicit
``target_data_file_id: null`` means "a new data file".

ListNotesIn.title: ListNotesIn
ListNotesIn.description:
Which words to add: these ones, or a whole lesson, or one heading of one.

A heading is the bulk gesture this app has — it is how the textbook prints a
set, and practice can already take one on its own.

ListOut.title: ListOut
ListOut.description: A named set of words, and whether its focus is still running.

ListPatchIn.title: ListPatchIn
ListPatchIn.description:
Every field optional, and null means *clear it* rather than *leave it*.

Ending a focus is setting ``focus_until`` to null, so the two cannot be the
same thing: which fields were actually sent is what tells them apart.

ListWordsOut.title: ListWordsOut
ListWordsOut.description: The list itself, and the words on it in the shape a search result has.

MasteryOut.title: MasteryOut
MasteryOut.description: One category of the mastery bars, counting everything under it.

MasteryRuleOut.title: MasteryRuleOut
MasteryRuleOut.description:
The thresholds the buckets are drawn at, so the page can say what it means.

Sent rather than duplicated in the client, because these are the numbers a
reader will ask about and there must be one answer to that question.

NoteHitOut.title: NoteHitOut
NoteHitOut.description:
One note as a search result lists it — a word, not a direction.

Note-shaped on purpose: a card is one way round, and what you searched for
was the word. ``forward`` and ``reverse`` are how well each direction is
known, and are null only for a direction the note has no card for.

NoteIn.title: NoteIn
NoteIn.description: A note as the editor sends it. Unset fields are left alone on a patch.

NoteOut.title: NoteOut
NoteOut.description:
A row of the grid editor. Mirrors the data-file note, plus what only the
database knows: how many cards it has and whether it has been archived.

PracticeResolved.title: PracticeResolved
PracticeResolved.description: And what that comes to once the tree above it has been applied.

PracticeSet.title: PracticeSet
PracticeSet.description: What a category says about practice itself. ``None`` means "ask my parent".

RelatedOut.title: RelatedOut
RelatedOut.description:
One other word in the collection, and what it has to do with this one.

There are no antonyms here and cannot be: nothing in a note records that one
word is the opposite of another. ``same-heading`` is what stands in for it,
because a textbook prints 위 beside 밑 for exactly that reason.

WeakCardOut.title: WeakCardOut
WeakCardOut.description: A card on the weak list, with the reason it is on it.

WordOut.title: WordOut
WordOut.description:
One note as a list of words shows it: ``prompt`` is the front.

``card_key`` and ``direction`` name the direction holding it in its bucket.
